deepdive.divline: - Capex funded INR 335cr debt + balance internal accruals; **no equity dilution**. FY27-end net debt ~INR 350-360cr

profile.entities: Filatex India Ltd (parent); subsidiary referred to as "Ecosis" / "Texfil" (textile-to-textile recycling specialty business)
profile.mgmt: Madhu Sudhan Bhageria (Chairman & MD); Ashok Chauhan (Chief Visionary Officer); Nitin Agarwal (CFO); Vedansh Bhageria (VP – Corporate Strategy)

bull_bear.body: - Capex funded INR 335cr debt + balance internal accruals; **no equity dilution**. FY27-end net debt ~INR 350-360cr. ROE ~12.96% (target +100-200 bps if normalized). Disciplined, return-driven (insists ≥12% to justify reinvestment).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Chinese imports / dumping:** post-QCO-revocation (Nov) import surge compressed margins; QCO/anti-dumping protection removed; future depends on relative China pricing.
- **Polyester spread compression:** near EBITDA-neutral on current spreads; crude/geopolitical volatility (Iran-Israel-US, Strait of Hormuz) the key swing factor.
- **Demand:** downstream destocking/postponement; price-fall fear; weak April-May seasonality + labor migration.
- **MEG/PTA import dependence**, forex (rupee slide, unhedged), logistics/freight, migrant labor availability, recycling plant ramp/client approval execution risk.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Candid and conservative. Openly acknowledged "caught on the wrong foot" on forex and that Q4/current spreads are EBITDA-neutral. Chose YoY framing to avoid flattering/misleading QoQ optics. Bullish medium-term ("golden years for polyester once war stops") but refused FY27 firm revenue guidance citing war. Emphasized recycling as differentiated technological moat while staying deliberately conservative on its EBITDA guide.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- March reported profit flattered by inventory/stock profit; underlying March EBITDA ~neutral.
- Recycling moat = "waste-to-chip" technology, NOT chip-to-yarn (commoditized) — strategy is to **sell chips**, not forward-integrate into yarn (keeps top line lighter but margins/tech-edge concentrated).
- Customers at zero RM inventory → sharp demand snapback risk/optionality once fear clears (INR 8-12/kg spread recovery possible).
- Short-term PTA/MEG duty relief (till June) had limited on-ground impact due to long import cycles.
- Domestic PTA plants initially priced at landed-import parity — savings only emerge once PTA becomes structurally surplus in India.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- Capex funded via internal accruals plus structured debt, explicitly with the aim of keeping leverage contained.
- Carries AA- long-term and A1+ short-term credit ratings.
- Strong liquidity and balance sheet allowed the company to hold inventory prudently through the price-normalisation period without compromising ongoing capex commitments.
- Returns have been improving — ROCE 11.76% (FY23) to 14.90% (FY26) and ROE 8.23% to 12.96% over the same period; the deck makes no dividend commentary.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Polyester yarn demand robust through Q3 FY26; disrupted Q4 by geopolitical/crude shock. Downstream (fabric/garment) postponing purchases — fear of price crash if war ends. Customers holding **zero RM inventory**, slightly elevated finished-goods inventory.
- Recovery "starting this month" (early May); labor migration (LPG cylinder cost spike, West Bengal & other elections) hurt April-May but labor returning by mid/end-May.
- Polyester non-discretionary; no substitution risk — cotton/alternatives 50-100%+ costlier. Slowdown framed as cyclical/sentiment-driven, not structural.
business.title: Demand

business.body: - Core is filament yarn (POY/FDY/DTY) + chips; ~1 lakh MT/quarter capacity, scaling to ~470,000 MT total after Sept brownfield. Capex tilts mix toward higher-margin FDY/DTY/PFY. Chips: recycling Greenfield end-product is **chip** (not yarn); yarn conversion done in existing/new facilities only if customer requires.
business.title: Segment (POY/FDY/DTY/chips)

business.body:
- China capacity rationalization (closing inefficient plants) + Sec.301 tariffs → India polyester/yarn exporters ⭐ (incl. Filatex).
- India-EU FTA zero-duty → Indian textile/recycled-yarn exporters ✅.
- Domestic PTA surplus (GAIL/IOC/RIL) → downstream Indian polyester producers (margin relief) ✅.

---
business.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries

business.body:
- Amongst the top 5 Polyester Filament Yarn (PFY) producers in India, with a fully integrated melt-to-yarn value chain running polymerisation to chips to POY/FDY/DTY, and over 30 years of operating experience.
- Claims first-mover status as the first PFY player in India doing true textile-to-fibre recycling, backed by a granted patent, a DSIR-approved R&D centre and a proven 1 MT/day pilot plant.
- Deck frames the model as a barbell: the core PFY business provides steady income while the new circular businesses drive innovation and upside, transitioning Filatex to a repeatable-growth materials platform.
- Argues most global peers in chemical textile-to-textile recycling remain at R&D or pilot stage, leaving no meaningful commercial-scale depolymerisation capacity globally and demand for virgin-grade circular polyester exceeding supply.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Subsidiary/MoU] ECOSIS (Filatex subsidiary) signed MoUs with American & Efird Global LLC (A&E Threads) and Decathlon India for trials of high-quality textile-to-textile recycled polyester, giving early commercial validation and access to one of the world's largest industrial thread manufacturers.
- [Policy] Removal of customs duties on PTA and MEG effective 2 April 2026 for three months (benefit in effect till 15 July 2026) provided near-term raw-material cost relief.
- [Trade] India-EU FTA (removing ~10-12% duty on MMF garments) and reduction of US tariffs on Indian textiles from 50% to 18% position India favourably vs Vietnam (~20%), Bangladesh (~19%) and China (~20%+).
- [Supply chain] Domestic PTA capacity additions from IOCL (1.2 MTPA), GAIL (1.2 MTPA) and RIL (3 MTPA) should progressively reduce import dependence, making the recent supply disruption transitional rather than structural.
- [Incentives] Filatex is aligned with PLI and NTTM priorities, with Dahej and Dadra facilities positioned to benefit from PM MITRA parks (₹4,445 Cr outlay) and FTA-led export access.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Per kg polyester: **860g PTA + 340g MEG**; PTA dominates cost (MEG <25%). PTA imported (mainly from China) at India landed parity + INR 8-10/kg freight/handling; MEG at import parity (structural import dependence — flagged as concern).
- Crude/petchem input cost +40-45% in Q4; pass-through limited → near EBITDA-neutral March. ~INR 13cr forex loss in Q4 (rupee slide; exposure INR 500-550cr; will hedge more going forward — hedging costs ~3.5-4%/$ ≈ INR 17.5-20cr/yr).
- Domestic PTA surplus expected to add ~1-1.5% margin; base polyester margin target 11-12%.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost (PTA/MEG, power)

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Mgmt deliberately framed YoY (not QoQ) — crude-driven volatility made Q3→Q4 non-comparable. Spread collapsed from ~INR 9/kg (Q3) to ~EBITDA-neutral (March/early May). FY26 full-year was record: EBITDA +34.5%, PAT +36.7%, ROE 12.96%. Q4 PAT dented by ~INR 13cr forex. Q1 FY27 volume guided −20-25% vs ~1 lakh MT/qtr. INR 690cr capex on track (most live by Sept; steam slips to mid-July). Recycling (Texfil/Ecosis) ≥30% EBITDA margin, INR 80-85cr conservative guide. No prior-quarter note on file for comparison.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Volume:** Q1 FY27 production to be cut **20-25% below the ~1 lakh MT/quarter** normal run-rate (demand-led, dynamic). Industry running ~60% utilization; **Filatex ~75%**.
- **Spread:** No firm guidance; near-term EBITDA-neutral until war/crude fear subsides; once normalized, ~INR 8-12/kg realization uplift possible. PTA domestic surplus to add **~1-1.5% margin** once GAIL+IOC operational → base polyester margin to move from ~8.33% toward **10%+ (target 11-12%)**.
- **Revenue:** Normal-year incremental ~INR 500cr → FY27 ~INR 4,500cr (only 6 months of new capacity) + ~INR 350-400cr from subsidiary; **FY28 ~INR 4,800cr (Filatex) + ~INR 400cr (Ecosis)**.
- **Value-added/recycling mix:** Textile-to-textile (Texfil/Ecosis) targeting **≥30% EBITDA margin**; conservative EBITDA guide ~INR 80-85cr at full capacity (recycle), capacity 75 TPD. Brownfield top line ~INR 500cr; Greenfield recycling top line ~INR 350-400cr.
- **Capex:** INR 690 cr total (debt ~INR 335cr, rest internal accruals — **no equity fundraise**). Net debt at FY27-end guided ~INR 350-360cr.
- **Incremental EBITDA from full capex program:** **INR 218-230 cr/year** (run-rate, post commissioning).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — explicit)

outlook.body:
- **Textile-to-textile recycling (Texfil/Ecosis):** glycolysis route converting end-of-life textiles (not PET bottles) into virgin-grade polymer/chips; qualifies for EU brand mandates. 75 TPD; recycled yarn realization **INR 180-225/kg vs virgin ~INR 120/kg**. In pilot/sample approval with brands (incl. Decathlon-type tie-ups); 2 clients approved, more in progress; full validation targeted by FY-end. Mgmt sees recycling as the primary future capex focus (virgin brownfield largely done at INR 235cr). Only one operational global peer (Cyclone, China); Carbios, Loop-Ester developing (Loop at ~2.5x Filatex's capex/ton).
- **India-EU FTA:** EU market $370bn; India moving to zero duty (from 10-12%); India + Vietnam advantaged, Bangladesh/China disadvantaged — fillip for recycled/export yarn.
- **Domestic PTA build-out (import substitution):** GAIL Mangalore (~July 2026), IOC Paradip (~Dec 2026) add ~2.4 MTPA; RIL +3.2 MTPA by end-CY27 → structural PTA surplus in 24 months.
- Steam monetization, renewable energy transition, Dahej automation (reduce labor dependence).
outlook.title: Growth / Optionality

deepdive.thesis: Filatex is a volume-led polyester filament yarn (POY/FDY/DTY) + chips manufacturer whose FY26 saw record EBITDA (+34.5% YoY to INR 346.5cr) despite flat volume, but Q4 was hit by a crude-driven petchem cost shock (Iran-Israel-US conflict, Strait of Hormuz disruption) that compressed spreads to near EBITDA-neutral exiting March; the medium-term equity story rests on a INR 690cr capex (value-added mix + brownfield + textile-to-textile recycling Greenfield + automation/steam/renewables) targeting INR 218-230cr incremental annual EBITDA, plus structural domestic PTA supply relief (GAIL/IOC/RIL) and India-EU FTA.
